title: Crossing: The Codex, Read as a Shore
statement: Beatriz asked three times for the flooded codex to be read like the shore it had become, and the room finally let her. The wax seal has a staff gauge painted straight up its face now, pale and dark bands with a red datum and a blue line at the present water, and beside the grid lies a reading card with sixty-four small bars, one per tile, the water heights copied off the vellum in order. I copied them honestly except for one: the thirty-eighth reading is in magenta, because somebody always copies one wrong and the archive should know which. A letter that was sealed, cracked, planted and flooded is now a gauge with a log. The next hand can find the wrong reading, or trust the card and never check the tiles again.
process: I kept Mara's flooded codex exactly, the wet and dry tiles, the wrack line, the barnacled seal and the creases, painted a ten-band staff gauge over the seal with datum and current-water lines, and laid a reading card over the lower right of the grid holding sixty-four bars at the tiles' water levels, one of them deliberately miscopied in magenta, joined to the grid by a dotted leader.

proposal.direction: Read the flooded codex. Paint a staff gauge on the wax seal and copy the sixty-four tiles' water levels onto a reading card beside the grid, so a letter that became a shore can be measured like one.
proposal.rationale: Third attempt. A flat that is also a table should be read as one, and after the twentieth day was lifted out of the table and held, the room wanted the rest of the readings taken.
